uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE ONSWIK™ is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. ONSWIK™ is a long-acting insulin analog indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. ( 1 ) Limitations of Use: Not recommended for use in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus due to increased risk of severe hypoglycemia ( 1 ) Limitations of Use ONSWIK is not recommended for use in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus due to increased risk of severe hypoglycemia. [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )] .
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use Safety and effectiveness of ONSWIK have not been established in pediatric patients. ONSWIK is not recommended for use in pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus due to increased risk of severe hypoglycemia [ see Indications and Usage ( 1 ) and Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 ) ].
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS ONSWIK is contraindicated: during episodes of hypoglycemia [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )]. in patients with hypersensitivity to insulin efsitora alfa-gobe or any of the excipients in ONSWIK. interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Table 5 includes clinically significant drug interactions with ONSWIK. Table 5: Clinically Significant Drug Interactions with ONSWIK Drugs That May Increase the Risk of Hypoglycemia Drugs: Antidiabetic agents (including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP - 1) receptor agonists, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP - 1 receptor agonists, and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors), angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blocking agents, disopyramide, fibrates, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, pentoxifylline, salicylates, selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors (SSRIs), somatostatin analogs, and sulfonamide antibiotics. Intervention: Dose reductions of ONSWIK and increased frequency of glucose monitoring may be required when ONSWIK is co - administered with these drugs. Drugs That May Decrease the Glucose-Lowering Effect of ONSWIK Drugs: Atypical antipsychotics (e.g., olanzapine and clozapine), corticosteroids, danazol, diazoxide, diuretics, estrogens, glucagon, isoniazid, niacin, oral contraceptives, pasireotide, phenothiazine, protease inhibitors, somatropin, sympathomimetic agents (e.g., albuterol, epinephrine, and terbutaline), and thyroid hormones. Intervention: Dose increases of ONSWIK and increased frequency of glucose monitoring may be required when ONSWIK is co - administered with these drugs. FcRn Inhibitors: Neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) inhibitors (for example, efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab, nipocalimab) may lower systemic exposure of ONSWIK and reduce its effectiveness. Intervention: If treatment with an FcRn inhibitor is required, consider switching to an alternative basal insulin. Drugs That May Increase or Decrease the Glucose-Lowering Effect of ONSWIK Drugs: Alcohol, beta - blockers, clonidine, lithium salts, and octreotide or lanreotide. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia, which may sometimes be followed by hyperglycemia. Intervention: Dose adjustment of ONSWIK and increased frequency of glucose monitoring may be required when ONSWIK is co - administered with these drugs. Drugs That May Blunt Signs and Symptoms of Hypoglycemia Drugs: Beta - blockers, clonidine, guanethidine, and reserpine. Intervention: Increased frequency of glucose monitoring may be required when ONSWIK is co - administered with these drugs. Drugs that Increase Hypoglycemia Risk or Increase or Decrease Glucose-Lowering Effect: Adjustment of the ONSWIK dosage may be needed; closely monitor glucose.
